title: Private VPC — CISO/CSO ask matrix + email templates (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Short working doc to consolidate CISO/CSO-focused asks, control-plane language we should use/avoid, negotiation levers, and ready-to-send email snippets for AE/SEs when engaging regulated prospects. Intended for SDRs->AEs and Solutions Engs as a lightweight kit.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: CISO, CSO, Head of Infrastructure, Cloud Security Architects, Procurement security reviewers.
- Use cases: financial services PII processing, healthcare PHI inference, government data residency, sovereign cloud scenarios.
- Channel: discovery calls, procurement packet, security RFIs, executive briefings.

Quick exec summary (what matters to them):
1) Data locality and isolation: “Can you prove my customer data never leaves our VPC?”
2) Control plane visibility & trust model: “Who can see metadata/metrics, and where is the control plane hosted?”
3) Auditability and evidence: SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS/HSM proof, network controls for audits.
4) Operational ownership: clear SLOs, incident playbooks, and rollback/fallback behavior.
5) Legal/contractual protections: DPA, indemnities, and breach notification timing.

Decision triggers (signals that accelerate an opportunity):
- Customer mentions regulated vertical, external audit requirement, or strict vendor isolation (e.g., banking core systems).
- Security RFP/RFI issued or procurement asks for on-prem/VPC options.
- Risk team requests dedicated control plane or proof of separation.

Message pillars (short, repeatable):
- "Control plane, your choice": You can run the control plane in Redwood-managed VPC, customer VPC with Redwood agents, or fully air-gapped on-prem — same API surface and rollout controls.
- "Observable & provable": Deliverables: audit logs, token-level traces, and per-request routing records you can ingest into SIEM.
- "Fail-safe fallbacks": Canary + automatic fallback policies to keep apps live if regional capacity is constrained.
- "No surprises on compute": Dedicated GPU pools + quotas ensure consistent latency and billing predictability.

Control-plane language (recommended phrasing):
- Use: "customer-managed control plane", "control-plane-in-VPC", "cryptographic key ownership (KMS/HSM)", "audit-ready logs with export hooks", "RBAC + SCIM provisioning support".
- Avoid: vague terms like "partial isolation" or "we handle network security" — customers prefer explicit network/topology statements.

Specific claims we can make today (to verify before using externally):
- We support deploying the control plane into a customer VPC with private endpoints and no public egress for control traffic (subject to network checklist).
- KMS/HSM integration available for keys controlling model encryption and tokenization.
- Audit artifacts: SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 summary, and customizable audit log exports to customer SIEM.
(Engineering: validate current region coverage + on-prem packaging before sales commit.)

Buyer objections + suggested rebuttals (short scripts):
1) "We can't allow an external control plane — risk of metadata leakage"
  - Rebuttal: "We offer a customer-managed control plane option that you can deploy in your VPC. Control plane components run on nodes you own; Redwood provides orchestration agents only. All control traffic can be routed over private peering with no public egress. We can show architecture diagrams and run a tabletop with your network team."
2) "How do you prove you didn't touch our keys/data?"
  - Rebuttal: "We integrate with your KMS/HSM. You retain cryptographic key ownership and can rotate/revoke keys at any time. For high assurance customers we keep a key-handover audit trail for procurement review."
3) "What happens on incident — will you access our data?"
  - Rebuttal: "Access to control-plane logs and metrics is scoped via RBAC and audit-logged. In emergency scenarios, we require customer approval (contracted emergency access) and produce post-incident reports. We also support predetermined runbooks so most incidents are mitigated without operator access."
4) "Pricing and hidden fees for private deployments."
  - Rebuttal: "We provide clear reserved capacity contracts; pricing levers are: committed GPU hours, data egress allowances, and premium SRE support. For procurement we can provide a price waterfall and example TCO vs hosted API for representative workloads."

Negotiation levers (what Sales can offer):
- Technical: longer onboarding windows, free proof-of-concept run hours, architecture/design workshop with Solutions Eng.
- Commercial: single-year committed capacity discounts, capped overage rates, optional premium SLA credits.
- Legal/compliance: tailored DPA addendum, tighter incident notification windows, pre-agreed audit windows.

Competitive posture (notes for quick read on calls):
- Competitor A (big cloud managed endpoint): cheap and simple, but control plane is cloud-managed and multi-tenant. They lose to us on guaranteed isolation and per-request observability.
- Competitor B (open-source self-hosted runtimes): total control but large ops burden. We win on unified API, simpler rollouts, and SRE-backed packages.
- Competitor C (specialized inference vendor): similar dedicated capacity but limited integrations (no KMS/HSM) and poor audit artifact maturity.

Procurement checklist (what security/procurement typically asks for):
- SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 attestation copies.
- DPA and data residency statements.
- Network topology diagram + expected ports/IP ranges.
- KMS/HSM integration details and key ownership model.
- Incident notification and escalation matrix.
- Pen test summary or remediation commitments.

Sample email snippets (AE -> CISO intro, short):
- Intro to schedule security architecture review:
  "Hi <Name>,
  We talked with <POC> about deploying Redwood in a customer-managed VPC to keep inference workloads inside your network. Do you have 30 minutes this week to walk through our control-plane topology, KMS integration, and audit artifacts so we can confirm it meets your standard? Happy to include our lead SE and architect.
  Thanks,
  <AE>"

- Procurement submission cover (attach artifact list):
  "Hi <Procurement>,
  Attached: SOC2 Type II summary, draft DPA, and our network checklist. Please confirm a time to review; we can iterate on the DPA terms and provide a security workshop for your team.
  Best,
  <AE>"

Call prep bullets for SEs (what to bring to a CISO call):
- Bring: control-plane architecture diagram (VPC option + no-public-egress flow), KMS sequence diagram, sample audit log, incident playbook excerpt.
- Ask: what controls does their audit team require, do they need on-site installation or an MTU-based appliance, and who is the procurement/security contact?

Open questions / engineering check items (TL;DR for product/eng):
- Confirm fully air-gapped on-prem packaging: which compute appliance images exist today and what the install timeline is.
- Confirm per-region availability of customer-managed control plane and required network prereqs (private peering vs. VPN).
- Export formats and retention defaults for audit logs (S3, Event Hubs, Splunk forwarder).
- KMS/HSM vendors we support (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, Thales) and whether HSM-backed envelopes are fully supported.

Artifacts to include in security packet (attach as links in final kit):
- SOC2 Type II (redacted)
- ISO27001 summary
- Network topology template
- Onboarding runbook + sample timeline
- Example SLO/SLA language for dedicated capacity

Suggested next steps (immediate):
- SEs: bake the control-plane diagram variant for VPC+on-prem into the customer pitch deck (owner: Ethan).
- Legal: draft a DPA appendix that explicitly covers customer-managed control plane and emergency access terms (owner: Mariana).
- Product: confirm availability table for on-prem appliance and region coverage (owner: Liam).
- GTM: create a short one-pager "Control plane ownership options" for AE use (owner: Aisha).

Notes to self / rough ideas (do not publish yet):
- Could offer a 3-tier control-plane packaging: co-managed (Redwood infra + customer VPC peering), customer-hosted control plane (agents only), and on-prem appliance. Price and SLA bands map to tiers.
- Consider a short customer attestation form to speed procurement: quick checkbox of required artifacts they need for security sign-off.
- Build a diagnostics export that security teams can run themselves during POC for independent verification.

End of draft.

Attachments we should generate before publishing: control-plane VPC diagram (v1), sample DPA clause for control-plane, one-pager pricing bands for private deployments.
